entry.title: Decide your worth!
entry.content:
Decide your worth!

Ones(your) worth is not something that can be measured by numbers, titles, or external validation. It is an intrinsic truth, deeply rooted within you — something only you can fully recognize and understand. While the world may try to define you through metrics, comparisons, or material achievements, the essence of value goes far beyond such superficial measures. You alone have the power to perceive and honor your worth beyond any societal constructs. But how do you truly judge your value? This is a deeply personal journey, one that no one else can undertake for you. When reflect on this, you will notice how many people go through life unaware of the impact their words or actions on others. They might think they’re being funny when making cutting remarks, completely oblivious to the harm or disrespect they may cause. Their lack of self-awareness blinds them to the weight of their intentions. In contrast, when you hold yourself in high regard — when you truly understand and respect your own value — you become acutely aware of your actions and words. When you strive to approach life with mindfulness, knowing that every sentence you spoke and every choice you made carries significance. Does this mean you are immune to mistakes? Not at all. Even when you value yourself deeply, you will still stumble and err. The difference lies in how you respond: if you acknowledge your missteps, reflect on them with honesty, and take responsibility for your actions. This self-awareness and accountability are what elevate your character and reinforce sense of worth.

True value is not about perfection; it’s about presence, integrity, and the courage to grow through every experience — good or bad. It’s about being fully conscious of who you are and strive to align your actions with your highest self. Only you can define what that means for you, and only you can live it authentically.

Decide your worth by yourself. Channelize, Analyze and Acknowledge.

entry.title: Smell of Rajasthan
entry.content:
In the hazy realm between sleep and wakefulness, the familiar symphony of an Indian kitchen gently pulls me from my dreams. It’s a winter weekend morning and the aroma of something special. The heavenly smell of bajre ki roti with ghee wafts through the house.

Time moves differently in those moments, stretching and contracting like a cat in a sunbeam. As noon approaches, the world outside seems to slow down, caught in the drowsy heat of the afternoon. But then, cutting through the sleepy silence, comes the tinkling of a bell. It’s the ice cream seller, and suddenly I used to run despite the oppressive heat. Holding in my hand, a bowl of wheat. A barter that feels both ancient and timeless. The artificial orange flavor in a uniquely nostalgic combination, hiding spot among the mustard seed sacks from the winter harvest. It’s was the secret place.

In this moment, past and present blur together, and I still wonder if in parallel universe, my childhood self is waiting for the sound of the ice cream seller’s bell to ring once more time before it stepping into fast pace life.

KIKI

entry.title: Fear of living an average life

link.title: Fear of living an average life

entry.content:
Fear of Living an Average Life

The Weight of living an Average Life — Every morning, I wake up to the same routine: the alarm blare, grabbing an Americano from the Cafe, and to sit in front of the screen. The world inside my phone screen buzzed with life, stories after stories. While scrolling through the screen, a gnawing fear gripped my heart. The fear of living an average life. I watched my friends chasing dreams, while i always felt tethered to mediocrity. Every day felt like a constant reminder of unfulfilled potential. This eventually led to mental exhaustion and a tired body. This daily battle within myself forced me to pause my mundane routine, and an epiphany led me to reevaluate my life’s direction. Journey of self-discovery, vowing to transform my once-average life into an extraordinary adventure began.

A glance in the past- I have possibly lived one of the best lives, People only imagine about having a such life and yet here i am who lived it. Perfect mental peace within myself while growing up, full of confidence in myself, flying without wings and with no fear of failing with the freedom to do whatever I wanted in a South Asian household. Surrounded by books of all kinds, which later became the platform of my deepest understanding of human behaviour. And yet i went through this mental torment at the age of 25. I was calculating every moment, feelings and circumstances which pushed me towards a terrible feeling and phobia of mundaneness. After analysing for a while, i have realised this feeling came from comparison. Comparing my worth and competence with everyone around me. When i was just taking my initial steps and everyone was about to finish the race. This comparison was completely unfair and was unkind to my soul. How did i even learnt to compare myself with others? Nobody taught me this at house, neither i have learnt this in school. I have leant this in the world of competitive people where everyone was running towards … what? To get that chair in the corner of some office but i was never made for it. I always knew I was not made for that.

And Yes! The journey begins. Journey of self reclaimation. To feel and hold that inner peace which i always had. Journey towards struggles which will be completely claimed by me in its entirety. This autumn bought me back to myself. ❤
